reasoning: EO 9886 substitutes "three years and one month" in paragraph 2(c) and adds that the order "shall cease to be in effect at such time, not later than the expiration of the period of three years and one month aforesaid" as the Secretary of Defense may provide in superseding regulations. Three years and one month from October 24, 1944 is November 24, 1947. The claim records that date inclusive and states the exclusive reading. Each extension was signed before the period then running expired (deadlines of Oct 24, 1945; Apr 24, 1946; Oct 24, 1946; Apr 24, 1947; June 24, 1947; Aug 24, 1947), so the order never lapsed in between, and every later-event date matches the signing date of its amending order. The claim discloses an earlier end through Secretary of Defense regulations as possible. It is the only route to an earlier end. No held source shows such a regulation or any other revocation, so the outer limit is the best supported date on held evidence, and the uncertainty is disclosed rather than hidden. The claim attaches the EO 9714 section 3 event to scope b-2 (item 2, the directive to prescribe regulations) and to b-dup2 (paragraph 2(b)), which are the correct scopes. Correction of my blind review: my blind finding that this event was attached to proviso EO:9492#b was my own misreading of a scope boundary in my output. The planted version attached the event exactly as the genuine one does. The inventory of eight scopes is complete. Savings (none_after_bounded_search) and the descriptions of the searches are accurate. One minor point needs no correction: EO 9840 does not name paragraph 2(c), but the substituted words occur only there.
